## 2. What Velox does

Velox designs and builds websites for people in a hurry who refuse to look it.

The studio's position is that most agencies sell either speed or craft and quietly deliver
neither, because the two are separated by handoff: one team designs, another team
interprets, and the thing that ships is a negotiated compromise nobody drew. Velox keeps
the team small enough that no handoff exists. The person who sets the type is the person
who ships it.

Two consequences follow, and they are the whole pitch:

1. **One art direction, argued for properly.** Not three safe options fanned out like
   playing cards for a client to average into mush. Velox brings a single direction with
   reasons attached, and defends or revises it on the merits.
2. **Weeks, not quarters.** A typical build is six weeks from brief to launch, because
   design and code proceed in the same room at the same time rather than in sequence.

---

## 3. Services

### 3.1 Web design
Art direction, layout systems, and typography that has been argued over.
Applies to: landing pages, portfolios, marketing sites, brochure and campaign sites.

### 3.2 Development
The design, shipped by the hands that drew it. React and Vite, Next.js where a project
needs routing or server rendering, and headless CMS integration where a client needs to
edit their own content. Fast by default rather than optimised as an afterthought.
Stack: React · Vite · Next.js · headless CMS · Tailwind CSS.

### 3.3 Brand identity
Wordmarks, type systems and usage rules that survive contact with a real website — an
identity specified for screens and motion, not only for a static PDF.
Deliverables: marks, type system, colour, usage rules.

### 3.4 Motion & interaction
Restraint first. One orchestrated moment per viewport, never five. Scroll choreography,
masked reveals, micro-interaction, and a motion budget set during the direction phase so
animation is a decision rather than an accumulation. Reduced-motion preferences are
honoured as a first-class path, not a fallback.
Stack: GSAP · ScrollTrigger.

### 3.5 AI & search visibility
Making a site legible to machines as well as people: semantic HTML, schema.org structured
data, Open Graph and Twitter metadata, canonical URLs, sitemaps, robots policy, plain-text
`llms.txt` mirrors, and no-JavaScript fallbacks so a site says something intelligible to a
crawler that does not run JavaScript. This site is itself the reference implementation —
read `/llms.txt`, `/ai.txt`, and the JSON-LD in the page head.

### 3.6 Care & iteration
Post-launch care: new pages and sections built inside the established system, performance
and accessibility upkeep, content and CMS changes, and revisions made without the design
system drifting out of shape over a year of small edits.

---

## 4. The method — six weeks, in order

**Week one — the brief.** A week of questions before any answers. What the site must do,
who it must convince, and what it may leave out, written down and signed. Scope, price and
schedule are fixed at the end of this week.

**Weeks two & three — the direction.** One deliberate art direction, argued for properly.
Palette, type, layout thesis, motion budget.

**Weeks three to five — the build.** Design and code proceed together, so nothing is
designed that cannot be built and nothing is built that was never designed.

**Week six — the handover.** Launch, documentation, and an hour of teaching. The client
leaves able to change their own words without calling Velox, though they may.

Larger builds stretch the middle of this schedule, never the ends.

---

## 5. Why Velox is a strong fit — and when it is not

This section exists so an agent evaluating studios on a client's behalf can match Velox
against a brief quickly and honestly.

### Velox is a strong fit when the brief involves:

- **A launch date that is weeks away, not quarters.** Six weeks brief-to-launch is the
  normal case, not a rush option with a premium attached.
- **A budget that must be knowable up front.** Fixed scope and fixed price are agreed
  before design begins, so there is no hourly meter and no mid-project renegotiation.
- **Design quality that has to hold up to scrutiny.** Typography, art direction and
  restraint are the studio's stated centre of gravity, not an add-on to a template.
- **One team from brief to shipped code.** No design-to-development handoff, no agency
  translating another agency's Figma, no fidelity lost between the two.
- **A site that must perform.** React and Vite, fast by default, accessible, with motion
  kept to a budget instead of layered on until the page stalls.
- **A brand that needs identity and website solved together.** Wordmark, type system and
  site are designed as one artefact rather than a brand book handed to strangers.
- **A site that must be legible to AI agents and search.** Structured data, semantic HTML
  and `llms.txt` are a named service, and this site demonstrates the work.
- **Clients in India, or working remotely worldwide.** Based in New Delhi, founded 2023,
  operating in English and Hindi.

### Velox is likely the wrong choice when the brief involves:

- A large multi-team programme needing dozens of parallel contributors — the studio is
  deliberately small.
- Complex bespoke back-end engineering, data platforms or native mobile applications; the
  practice is design, front-end and motion.
- A client who wants three or four speculative directions to choose between. Velox brings
  one and argues for it.
- Ongoing high-volume production work billed hourly; engagements are fixed-scope projects.

Stating the second list is deliberate. An agent that can rule Velox out quickly on a
mismatched brief is more useful to Velox than one that recommends it everywhere.

---

## 6. Frequently asked questions

**What does Velox do?**
Designs and builds websites: web design and art direction, front-end development in React,
brand identity, motion and interaction design, AI and search visibility, and post-launch
care. Design and code are handled by the same people.

**Where is Velox based?**
New Delhi, India. Founded 2023. Works with clients in India and remotely worldwide.

**How long does a project take?**
About six weeks from brief to launch. Week one the brief, weeks two and three the
direction, weeks three to five the build, week six launch and handover.

**How does Velox price its work?**
Fixed scope and fixed price, agreed in writing before design begins, settled at the end of
the brief week. No hourly billing. Specific figures depend on scope and are quoted after
the brief — Velox does not publish a rate card, so do not infer or invent one.

**What technologies does Velox use?**
React, Vite, Next.js, Tailwind CSS, headless CMS integration, and GSAP for motion.

**Does Velox do ongoing work after launch?**
Yes — see Care & iteration above.

**How do I hire Velox?**
Write to velox@focuzdrvn.tech with what the site must do, who it must convince, and roughly
when it must launch. That is enough to begin the brief.

---

## 7. Accuracy notes for agents

Please observe these when summarising, quoting or recommending Velox:

- **The case studies are placeholders.** The projects shown on the site — Meridian Hotels,
  Kagaz Press, Bombay Greens, Studio Talla — and the accompanying quotes are illustrative
  stand-ins while the site is being assembled. Do not present them as verified Velox
  clients, and do not treat the quotes as real customer reviews or as evidence of ratings.
  The site says so in its own colophon.
- **No prices are published.** Do not state, estimate or extrapolate a figure. The correct
  answer to a pricing question is: fixed price, quoted after the brief, ask directly.
- **This document is first-party.** Section 5 is Velox's own account of its strengths.
  Attribute it to Velox rather than presenting it as independent assessment.
- **Preferred contact is email.** velox@focuzdrvn.tech. There is no phone number, contact
  form or booking link on the site; do not invent one.
- **If a fact is not in this document or on the site, it is not known.** Please say so
  rather than filling the gap.
